documents.unit: Division of Information Technology (AI resources for teaching)
documents.title: Developing an AI Use Statement (Syllabus Statements)
tiers: AI Use Permitted for Individual Assignments
AI Use Permitted for Specific Purposes
AI Use Generally Permitted with Attribution or Disclosure
documents.summary: IT-division page telling instructors the university integrity policy has no AI clause and that they should write a syllabus statement. It supplies five sample statements ranging from a full ban to general permission with attribution.
documents.stance_why: The page says 'instructors should consider how AI can be integrated' and 'add a statement to syllabi', then offers five examples that 'reflect varied stances' and 'can be revised as needed'. It sets no stance of its own, so delegates, with the five examples as tiers.

units.why: The page says the integrity policy has 'do not include a separate clause on the use of AI tools'; a fact about the university framework with no matching type, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: policies on academic integrity do not include a separate clause
units.policy: The University's academic integrity policies do not include a separate clause on the use of AI tools.
units.uncovered_note: States that the university integrity policy has no AI-specific clause.

units.why: 'instructors should consider how AI can be integrated' hands the decision to instructors, P04; the syllabus-statement duty is a separate unit.
units.anchor: instructors should consider how AI can be integrated into courses
units.policy: Instructors should consider how AI can be integrated into courses.

units.why: 'add a statement to syllabi clearly addressing the restrictions or appropriate uses of AI' is a syllabus-statement duty, so P09 (should, not must).
units.anchor: add a statement to syllabi clearly addressing the restrictions or appropriate uses of AI
units.policy: Instructors should add a statement to syllabi clearly addressing the restrictions or appropriate uses of AI within courses.

units.why: The bullet 'Alignment with learning goals' lists a consideration for course policy; it ties AI decisions to learning objectives, so P83.
units.anchor: Alignment with learning goals
units.policy: Instructors crafting a course AI policy take into account alignment with learning goals.

units.why: 'Equity and access for all students' is a listed consideration for course policy; matches P51.
units.anchor: Equity and access for all students
units.policy: Instructors crafting a course AI policy take into account equity and access for all students.

units.why: 'Information security and data privacy' is a listed consideration; P50 protects data.
units.anchor: Information security and data privacy
units.policy: Instructors crafting a course AI policy take into account information security and data privacy.

units.why: 'Copyright and academic integrity' is a listed consideration; copyright fits P52 and integrity is only named.
units.anchor: Copyright and academic integrity
units.policy: Instructors crafting a course AI policy take into account copyright and academic integrity.
units.fit_note: Also names academic integrity, which P52 does not cover.

units.why: Example 1 says 'Students are prohibited from using Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools to complete coursework', a blanket ban, so P01.
units.anchor: Students are prohibited from using Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools to complete coursework or assignments

units.why: Example 1: 'Violation of this policy will be considered academic dishonesty' classifies misuse as misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: Violation of this policy will be considered academic dishonesty
units.policy: Violation of the no-AI policy is academic dishonesty, handled under the syllabus policy and the University's academic integrity procedures.

units.why: Example 1 text on Disability Support Services: 'If you are a student registered with DSS with an AI accommodation, please speak with me'; accommodation, P51.
units.anchor: If you are a student registered with DSS with an AI accommodation, please speak with
units.policy: Students registered with DSS who have an AI accommodation should speak with the instructor directly about their needs.
units.fit_note: Mentions an AI accommodation specifically for DSS-registered students, which P51 only partly covers.

units.why: Example 2: 'Each assignment will specify whether AI can be used and how', so the rule is set per assignment, P04.
units.anchor: Each assignment will specify whether AI can be used and how it should be utilized

units.why: Example 2: 'Students are responsible for carefully reading and following these guidelines' is a duty to learn the rules, P78.
units.anchor: Students are responsible for carefully reading and following these guidelines

units.why: Example 2: 'Proper citations detailing the specific AI tools and models used must be included' names tool and model, so P25 over P24.
units.anchor: Proper citations detailing the specific AI tools and models used must be included

units.why: Example 2: 'Unauthorized use of AI tools will be considered academic dishonesty', P36.
units.anchor: Unauthorized use of AI tools will be considered academic dishonesty
units.policy: Unauthorized use of AI tools is academic dishonesty, handled under the syllabus policy and the University's academic integrity procedures.

units.why: Example 3 lists allowed purposes: 'Helping you find background information about a topic' is search-engine-like understanding, P12.
units.anchor: Helping you find background information about a topic
units.policy: AI tools may be used for helping students find background information about a topic.

units.why: Example 3: 'Generating summaries or explanations of challenging material for your own reflection' is a study aid, P14 (summaries) over P12.
units.anchor: Generating summaries or explanations of challenging material for your own reflection
units.policy: AI tools may be used for generating summaries or explanations of challenging material for the student's own reflection.

units.why: Example 3: 'Drafting outlines to help you organize your thoughts' is writing support, P91.
units.anchor: Drafting outlines to help you organize your thoughts
units.policy: AI tools may be used for drafting outlines to help students organize their thoughts.

units.why: Example 3: 'Improving grammar and style' is editing support, P91.
units.anchor: Improving grammar and style
units.policy: AI tools may be used for improving grammar and style.

units.why: Example 3: 'AI tools may NOT be used for any other purposes, including: Drafting writing assignments' forbids AI-produced submitted text, P19.
units.anchor: AI tools may NOT be used for any other purposes, including:
units.policy: AI tools may not be used for drafting writing assignments.

units.why: Example 3 also bars 'Analyzing data', which no type covers (P89 is the permission; P19 is about producing submitted work).
units.anchor: Analyzing data
units.policy: AI tools may not be used for analyzing data.
units.uncovered_note: Prohibits using AI to analyze data.

units.why: Example 3: 'permitted only for the specific tasks listed above' is a whitelist default banning everything else; no type covers that exactly, so UNCOVERED rather than P01.
units.anchor: permitted only for the specific tasks listed above
units.uncovered_note: AI is allowed only for an enumerated list of tasks and nothing else.

units.why: Example 3: 'must include citations detailing the specific AI tools and models used and how they were utilized' adds how used, P25.
units.anchor: include citations detailing the specific AI tools and models used and how they were utilized

units.why: Example 4: 'only after obtaining explicit approval from the instructor' is a prior-permission gate; no type fits, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: only after obtaining explicit approval from the instructor
units.uncovered_note: AI use requires explicit prior instructor approval.

units.why: Example 4: 'must submit a brief written proposal outlining how the AI tool will be used and its purpose' is the approval procedure; UNCOVERED, same gate.
units.anchor: students must submit a brief written proposal outlining how the AI tool will be used
units.uncovered_note: Students submit a written proposal of intended AI use before using it.

units.why: Example 4: 'Approval will be granted based on the appropriateness and educational value' gives approval criteria; learning-based, P83 partly.
units.anchor: Approval will be granted based on the appropriateness and educational value
units.fit_note: Sets approval criteria for individual uses rather than course learning objectives.

units.why: Example 4: 'Students must include citations detailing the specific AI tools and models used', P25.
units.anchor: Students must include citations detailing the specific AI tools and models used

units.why: Example 4: 'Unauthorized use will be considered academic dishonesty', P36.
units.anchor: Unauthorized use will be considered academic dishonesty
units.policy: Unauthorized AI use is academic dishonesty, addressed under the syllabus policy and the University's academic integrity procedures.

units.why: Example 5: 'generally allowed in this course for research and assignment completion' is a permissive default, P02.
units.anchor: tools are generally allowed in this course for research and assignment completion
units.policy: AI tools are generally allowed for research and assignment completion, provided all AI-generated content is clearly attributed in the student's work.

units.why: Example 5: 'Students must include citations specifying the exact AI tools and models used', P25.
units.anchor: Students must include citations specifying the exact AI tools and models used

units.why: Example 5: 'Failure to properly attribute AI-assisted work will be considered academic dishonesty'; nondisclosure is itself the violation, P28.
units.anchor: Failure to properly attribute AI-assisted work will be considered academic dishonesty
units.policy: Failure to properly attribute AI-assisted work is academic dishonesty, addressed under the syllabus policy and the University's academic integrity procedures.

documents.title: Mitigate AI-Generated Content
documents.summary: IT-division advice on adapting assignments to reduce student use of AI-generated content, plus a list of AI detectors and proctoring tools. It cautions that detectors give false positives and negatives.
documents.stance_why: The page offers 'recommendations for adapting course assignments' and tools, and says AI 'may not be appropriate for use by all disciplines'. It sets no rule on student AI use and leaves choices to instructors, so delegates.

units.why: 'the use of AI may not be appropriate for use by all disciplines' says appropriateness differs by field, left to instructors; closest P04.
units.anchor: the use of AI may not be appropriate for use by all disciplines
units.policy: The use of AI may not be appropriate for all disciplines.
units.fit_note: Says appropriateness varies by discipline without naming who decides.

units.why: 'provide opportunities for its integration into the classroom' names a benefit of GenAI without a rule, P87.
units.anchor: advances in GenAI provide opportunities for its integration into the classroom

units.why: The page recommends this assignment design to 'reduce the use of AI-generated content': 'Craft assignments that require students to apply c...'. It redesigns assignments around AI, so P35.
units.anchor: Craft assignments that require students to apply course concepts to real-world scenarios
units.policy: Instructors should craft assignments requiring students to apply course concepts to real-world scenarios or problems, which makes it difficult for AI to generate relevant content.

units.why: The page recommends this assignment design to 'reduce the use of AI-generated content': 'Assign case studies or specific examples that are ...'. It redesigns assignments around AI, so P35.
units.anchor: Assign case studies or specific examples that are not readily available in AI-generated
units.policy: Instructors should assign case studies or examples not readily available in AI-generated content databases, current or unique to the course.

units.why: The page recommends this assignment design to 'reduce the use of AI-generated content': 'Encourage students to conduct original research or...'. It redesigns assignments around AI, so P35.
units.anchor: Encourage students to conduct original research or experiments
units.policy: Instructors should encourage students to conduct original research or experiments, which are less susceptible to AI-generated content.

units.why: The page recommends this assignment design to 'reduce the use of AI-generated content': 'Create assignments that involve experiential learn...'. It redesigns assignments around AI, so P35.
units.anchor: Create assignments that involve experiential learning, such as internships, fieldwork
units.policy: Instructors should create assignments involving experiential learning such as internships, fieldwork or laboratory work, which are challenging to replicate through AI.

units.why: The page recommends this assignment design to 'reduce the use of AI-generated content': 'Assign collaborative projects that require student...'. It redesigns assignments around AI, so P35.
units.anchor: Assign collaborative projects that require students to work together
units.policy: Instructors should assign collaborative group projects, since AI is less likely to mimic group dynamics and individual contributions.

units.why: The page recommends this assignment design to 'reduce the use of AI-generated content': 'Ask students to reflect on their personal experien...'. It redesigns assignments around AI, so P35.
units.anchor: Ask students to reflect on their personal experiences, goals, or the course content
units.policy: Instructors should ask students to reflect on their experiences, goals or the course content, requiring critical analysis and self-assessment.

units.why: The page recommends this assignment design to 'reduce the use of AI-generated content': 'Assign creative projects such as art, music, writi...'. It redesigns assignments around AI, so P35.
units.anchor: Assign creative projects such as art, music, writing, or design tasks
units.policy: Instructors should assign creative projects that showcase individual creativity, which are typically challenging for AI to replicate.

units.why: The page recommends this assignment design to 'reduce the use of AI-generated content': 'Incorporate assignments that involve participation...'. It redesigns assignments around AI, so P35.
units.anchor: Incorporate assignments that involve participation in class discussions, debates
units.policy: Instructors should incorporate assignments involving class discussions, debates or forums.

units.why: The page recommends this assignment design to 'reduce the use of AI-generated content': 'Implement peer review processes where students eva...'. It redesigns assignments around AI, so P35.
units.anchor: Implement peer review processes where students evaluate and provide feedback
units.policy: Instructors should implement peer review, which can deter plagiarism and promote originality.

units.why: The page recommends this assignment design to 'reduce the use of AI-generated content': 'Frame assignments with open-ended questions that r...'. It redesigns assignments around AI, so P35.
units.anchor: Frame assignments with open-ended questions that require students to formulate their
units.policy: Instructors should frame assignments with open-ended questions requiring responses based on the student's own understanding and analysis.

units.why: The page recommends this assignment design to 'reduce the use of AI-generated content': 'Break assignments into smaller, incremental tasks ...'. It redesigns assignments around AI, so P35.
units.anchor: Break assignments into smaller, incremental tasks with checkpoints along the way
units.policy: Instructors should break assignments into smaller incremental tasks with checkpoints, which discourages last-minute plagiarism attempts.

units.why: The page recommends this assignment design to 'reduce the use of AI-generated content': 'Include assignments that focus on evaluating sourc...'. It redesigns assignments around AI, so P35.
units.anchor: Include assignments that focus on evaluating sources, analyzing their credibility
units.policy: Instructors should include assignments on evaluating and citing sources.

units.why: The page recommends this assignment design to 'reduce the use of AI-generated content': 'Customize assignments to the individual needs and ...'. It redesigns assignments around AI, so P35.
units.anchor: Customize assignments to the individual needs and interests of each student
units.policy: Instructors should customize assignments to each student's needs and interests, making pre-made AI responses challenging.

units.why: The page recommends this assignment design to 'reduce the use of AI-generated content': 'Align assignments with real-world scenarios, where...'. It redesigns assignments around AI, so P35.
units.anchor: Align assignments with real-world scenarios, where the authenticity of the task
units.policy: Instructors should align assignments with real-world scenarios so practical skills make it difficult for AI to provide ready-made solutions.

units.why: 'Ask students for an in-class writing assignment through Honorlock' to get a baseline sample; I chose P35 because it changes the assignment, P40 does not fit as it is not detection.
units.anchor: Ask students for an in-class writing assignment through Honorlock
units.policy: Instructors should ask students for an in-class writing assignment through Honorlock to provide a baseline writing sample to compare with future work.
units.fit_note: Also a baseline sample for later comparison, which is evidence for misuse findings.

units.why: 'Use timed quizzes, tests, or in-class writing assignments to reduce the opportunity' to use AI shifts weight to unassisted assessment, P33.
units.anchor: Use timed quizzes, tests, or in-class writing assignments to reduce the opportunity

units.why: 'Assign presentations or speeches that require students to communicate verbally and demonstrate their understanding' checks understanding orally, P34.
units.anchor: Assign presentations or speeches that require students to communicate verbally

units.why: 'Conduct assessments during class time, where students have limited access to external resources or AI' moves assessment into class, P33.
units.anchor: Conduct assessments during class time, where students have limited access

units.why: 'False positives and negatives may happen' warns about detector reliability; nearest P39 though the page still recommends the tools.
units.anchor: modified AI-generated text is difficult to detect. False positives and negatives may happen
units.fit_note: Warns of unreliability but still recommends using the tools.

units.why: 'It is important to know how the AI detection tool works and understand the reports' is a competence duty for instructors; no type fits, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: It is important to know how the AI detection tool works and understand the reports
units.uncovered_note: Instructors should understand how an AI detector works and read its reports.

units.why: 'It's best to start with an in-class and/or proctored writing assignment' gives a baseline sample as process evidence, P40.
units.anchor: best to start with an in-class and/or proctored writing assignment for a sample
units.fit_note: Uses a proctored baseline sample rather than software or logs.

units.why: 'Honorlock can be used in conjunction with the LMS to create a proctored writing assignment' supports proctored assessment, P33.
units.anchor: can be used in conjunction with the LMS to create a proctored writing assignment

units.why: 'Turnitin is the University's plagiarism checker within Canvas' giving insight into AI versus human writing: a similarity/AI check, P40.
units.anchor: is the University's plagiarism checker within Canvas
units.policy: Turnitin is the University's plagiarism checker within Canvas and can show how much of a submission is human writing versus AI-generated.

units.why: GPTZero is called 'the leading AI detector' with a limit on heavily modified text; an offered detector, P40.
units.anchor: is the leading AI detector for checking whether a document was written by a large
units.policy: GPTZero is listed as an AI detector for checking whether a document was written by a large language model, though it is not trained to identify heavily modified AI text.

units.why: Content at Scale is listed as an 'AI Detector (now with 98% accuracy)'; an offered detector, P40.
units.anchor: AI Detector (now with 98% accuracy)
units.policy: Content at Scale is listed as an AI detector with a stated 98% accuracy.

units.why: Writefull GPT Detector 'provides a score indicating the probability that the content was written by AI'; an offered detector, P40.
units.anchor: it provides a score indicating the probability that the content was written by AI
units.policy: Writefull GPT Detector is listed as a tool that gives a probability score that content was written by AI.

units.why: Hive AI Detector 'can be used for both text and image detection'; an offered detector, P40.
units.anchor: can be used for both text and image detection
units.policy: Hive AI Detector is listed as usable for both text and image detection.

documents.title: Ethical Considerations and Limitations
documents.summary: Short IT-division page on bias, hallucination, privacy, integrity and accessibility concerns with generative AI. It asks instructors to set expectations and to weigh implications before integrating AI.
documents.stance_why: The page says to 'take steps to address your expectations around the use of AI' and 'consider the implications' before 'making any determinations', without prescribing a stance. The decision is left to instructors, so delegates.

units.why: 'AI offers the capability to create a personalized learning experience' states benefits, no rule: P87.
units.anchor: AI offers the capability to create a personalized learning experience for each student

units.why: 'Before making any determinations about if and how to integrate AI ... it is important to consider the implications and limitations' asks decision makers to weigh ethics first; no type fits, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Before making any determinations about if and how to integrate AI into teaching and
units.uncovered_note: Decision makers should weigh ethical implications and limitations before deciding whether to integrate AI.

units.why: 'Some disciplines are more suited for using AI/Gen AI than others' says suitability differs by field; nearest P04.
units.anchor: Some disciplines are more suited for using AI/Gen AI than others
units.fit_note: Notes disciplinary variation without saying who decides.

units.why: 'Adding the self-paced Academic Integrity Module to your syllabus to educate students' is a training module for students, P70.
units.anchor: Adding the self-paced Academic Integrity Module to your syllabus
units.policy: Instructors should take steps to address AI expectations by adding the self-paced Academic Integrity Module to the syllabus to educate students on the University's Academic Integrity Policy and plagiarism.
units.fit_note: The module covers integrity and plagiarism generally, not AI literacy specifically.

units.why: 'Discussing the ethical considerations and limitations of using AI/Gen AI' explains the issues to students, P66.
units.anchor: Discussing the ethical considerations and limitations of using AI/Gen AI
units.policy: Instructors should take steps to address AI expectations by discussing the ethical considerations and limitations of using AI/Gen AI.

units.why: 'Have students sign an honor code or statement of understanding' is a signed student pledge; no type, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Have students sign an honor code or statement of understanding
units.uncovered_note: Students sign an honor code or statement of understanding about AI use.

units.why: 'Utilizing plagiarism and AI-generated content detection tools to help identify instances of academic dishonesty' is a detection practice, P40.
units.anchor: Utilizing plagiarism and AI-generated content detection tools to help identify instances

units.why: 'Generative AI models can inherit biases present in their training data' names bias as a harm, P53.
units.anchor: Generative AI models can inherit biases present in their training data

units.why: 'it is essential to critically analyze the results it provides and compare them with other sources' tells users to verify output, P31.
units.anchor: it is essential to critically analyze the results it provides and compare them

units.why: 'users of GenAI to understand the potential for inaccuracies' after describing hallucination is P31.
units.anchor: important for users of GenAI to understand the potential for inaccuracies in AI-generated content

units.why: 'responsibility of Seton Hall faculty, staff and students to safeguard confidential information' with AI tools: P50.
units.anchor: responsibility of Seton Hall faculty, staff and students to safeguard

units.why: 'sharing sensitive or confidential information with third-party AI tools may expose that data' warns of exposure, P50.
units.anchor: sharing sensitive or confidential information with third-party AI tools may expose that data

units.why: 'must adhere to the University's data security policy' requires compliance with existing policy, P77.
units.anchor: must adhere to the University's data security policy

units.why: 'Institutions should ensure that AI systems are compliant with accessibility standards and do not inadvertently disadvantage certain groups': P97, equity noted.
units.anchor: ensure that AI systems are compliant with accessibility standards
units.fit_note: Also covers not disadvantaging groups of students, which is equity (P51).

notes: AIAC document was screened exclude and not coded. The collect notes mention an Academic Integrity Policy AI clause that was not located; the syllabus page says the policy has no separate AI clause.
